factsAdvanced_en: The Czech Republic has the highest density of castles in the world, with over 2,000 registered castles and chateaux, earning it the nickname 'Castle Capital of the World'.
It holds the record for the highest beer consumption per capita globally, with citizens consuming an average of over 140 liters of beer each year.
Prague Castle is recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records as the largest ancient castle complex in the world, sprawling over an area of nearly 70,000 square meters.
The word 'robot' originated in the Czech language, first appearing in Karel Čapek's 1920 science fiction play 'R.U.R.' (Rossum's Universal Robots).
The modern soft contact lens was invented in 1961 by Czech chemist Otto Wichterle, who created the first lenses at home using a machine built from a children's construction set.
The country features one of the densest and best-marked hiking trail networks in the world, with over 40,000 kilometers of color-coded paths crisscrossing the landscape.

The Czech Republic is home to 17 UNESCO World Heritage sites, a remarkable number for its size, including the historic centers of Prague, Český Krumlov, and the unique Lednice-Valtice Cultural Landscape.
The city of Pilsen (Plzeň) is the birthplace of the Pilsner beer style, which was first brewed in 1842 and now accounts for more than two-thirds of all beer consumed worldwide.
